speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We need to strengthen our partnerships and collaboration to help more SMEs succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Liang Eng Hwa have asked about TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our TACs are important enablers in the transformation of industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have a good sense of what is happening among their members and have strong industry networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This allows them to effectively reach out and help more SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past decade, through the Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) programme, SPRING and IE have engaged about 40 TACs actively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They work on projects to support their members in capability upgrading and internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As an example, the Singapore Food Manufacturers' Association (SFMA) continues to build the international reputation of Singapore food products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It does so through activities, such as helping SMEs find new channels for their products in overseas markets, as well as marketing quality food products as tourism gifts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Miss Cheryl Chan also asked about our plans to support our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are working with the Federation of Merchants' Associations, Singapore (FMAS) to deepen their internal capabilities and rejuvenate our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: FMAS was recently awarded projects under our LEAD and LEAD+ programme to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of the projects FMAS will be working on is to help our heartland enterprises better align their business models to meet new demands of consumers and explore partnerships within the community for capability upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To start off, FMAS is conducting two pilot studies in Bedok and Ang Mo Kio to identify market needs and formulate precinct development plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In total, this project could benefit more than 2,500 heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har may wish to note that during the last Budget, we introduced SPRING's LEAD+ programme to raise the internal capabilities of TACs in four areas, namely, TAC's leadership, management, processes and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To date, seven TACs have been supported through LEAD+.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we will expand our outreach to more TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have received feedback from several smaller associations that they would like to embark on projects to help their members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But they say they lack the know-how or experience to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To help these TACs take the first step, we will support them in improving their internal systems and processes, as well as in implementing bite-size upgrading projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, we encourage TACs to collaborate with one another to reap greater benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such projects should have clear productivity enhancements or innovative outcomes that benefit a sizeable number of SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The full benefits of industry transformation cannot be felt if we have only a handful of progressive, creative SMEs in each industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These benefits can only be unleashed when the majority of SMEs participate fully in the transformation process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In this respect, we ask two things of SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If you have found forums, workshops or networking platforms provided by the MTI family to be useful, please spread the word.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If you have achieved success with a boost from our assistance schemes, please do not shy away from speaking up when invited or interviewed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will help contribute to a more collaborative business ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I recently attended the Turning Passion into Profits shareback event organised by the Singapore Productivity Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The aim was to help raise awareness about the resources and support ecosystem that F&B startups and microenterprises can tap on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I was very encouraged that several successful entrepreneurs came back to share their stories with others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One example was Ms Diana Teo, co-founder of WaaCow!.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a fast-casual restaurant retailing premium quality Japanese-inspired rice bowls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: She spoke very passionately about the assistance she received.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are many more Diana Teos out there, and their collective sharing will help many more entrepreneurs build better, more competitive businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The MTI family is committed to supporting them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We shall press on with our efforts to restructure the economy, even as we cope with the more immediate challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I have explained how we intend to do this through the ITMs, various initiatives to help our SMEs stay competitive, and working in closer partnership with our TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together, I am confident that our SMEs will emerge stronger and better prepared for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Our SMEs form the key pillar of our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: How can SMEs transform in the future economy is a key concern shared by the Government and our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government takes feedback from SMEs very seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These SME Centres have worked well to complement the SME Portal set up by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also actively enhancing the SME Portal with new features like Tech Depot, which provides technology and digital solutions suitable for SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I urge SMEs to fully utilise the SME Centres and SME Portal as the first point of contact for them to seek assistance and obtain information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Thirdly, SMEs interested in transformation have also said that they hope to receive more guidance on implementation, so as to avoid going through a lengthy process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Of course, instead of helping SMEs one by one, it is more effective to do it through the TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To get more SMEs on board various assistance schemes, the Government is also trying to enhance cooperation with the TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: FMAS embody the spirit of self-help and has strived to carve out a new path and inject vibrancy into neighbourhood businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I hope to see more SMEs tapping into and strengthening the TACs and their networks, explore faster and better ways to embark on their journey of transformation, to turn a new page not just for themselves but also for the Singapore economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to display some slides on the LED screens later on in my speech, please?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Several Members asked about the Government's efforts to help our companies and people adopt new technologies and internationalise.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Manufacturing continues to remain a key pillar for our economy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As highlighted by Mr Charles Chong, manufacturing creates good job opportunities for our people, contributes to productivity growth and generates positive spillovers to the rest of the economy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Having a manufacturing base also helps us capture opportunities and generate innovation which would otherwise take place overseas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Our push into advanced manufacturing will help strengthen the competitiveness and relevance of our manufacturing sector.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One key difference between advanced and traditional manufacturing is the digitalisation and automation of manufacturing operations and workflow processes, from receiving an order, all the way to the production on the factory floor.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Advanced manufacturing will enable companies, both large and small, to raise their productivity, as well as develop adjacent products, services and business models.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In turn, this will strengthen Singapore's leadership in key industrial clusters, such as aerospace and semiconductors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Miss Cheryl Chan observed, global leading manufacturers have been investing in the development and commercialisation of new manufacturing technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Miss Cheryl Chan may be happy to note that many of these players continue to remain keen to work with our public sector research institutes (RIs).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, aerospace heavy-weights Airbus and Honeywell have leveraged A*STAR's Aerospace Programme to better understand and minimise the causes of defects in aerospace components through additive manufacturing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Under the Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering (AME) (RIE) 2020 strategy, we will leverage partnerships with leading manufacturers to co-develop and deploy advanced manufacturing technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The goal is to enhance the competitiveness of our manufacturing sector and position our enterprises as solution providers of advanced manufacturing technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To this end, based on our established two "Model Factories" to allow companies, particularly our SMEs, to firstly, experience the technologies first-hand in a learning environment, without affecting their existing business operations and, secondly, to collaborate with stakeholders to test-bed and jointly develop innovative solutions for their processes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Each Model Factory is designed to support the different technological needs of companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A key feature of the Model Factory@SIMTech is a "live" pilot-scale production line that allows companies to gain hands-on experience of advanced manufacturing technologies, prior to full adoption.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SIMTech has also developed a suite of digital manufacturing solutions called the Manufacturing Control Tower (MCT) Platform which allows companies to have greater visibility and smarter management of their manufacturing operations through a central control platform that is easily accessible via a simple mobile app.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second Model Factory@ARTC will allow companies to test-bed the integration of smart, digital and advanced technologies with their existing manufacturing processes for better productivity and resource utilisation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Even as A*STAR is setting up these Model Factories I spoke about, one of our local enterprises has already started piloting SIMTech's MCT platform.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Precision engineering company CKE Manufacturing is making use of the MCT to monitor the performance of five of its shop-floor machines in real-time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Using a mobile app, CKE's staff are able to track the performance of the machines without having to physically inspect them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The pilot has enabled CKE to improve its manpower deployment by about 50% and optimise the utilisation of its machines.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: CKE is now looking at connecting all its machines to this MCT platform.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The technology changes that we are witnessing are global in nature and not unique to the manufacturing sector.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng noted, the biologics landscape is changing, too.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The biosimilars space is nascent and the regulatory environment is still evolving internationally.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What we do know is that innovator drugs, such as biosimilars, both require a strong regulatory environment, clinical development and manufacturing know-how to deliver safe and high-quality products to patients.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will continue to build core capabilities in R&D and the advanced manufacturing of biologics, in order to position Singapore well to capture investments arising from biologics, which includes biosimilars, regardless of the eventual market structure in this category of drugs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are confident that Singapore is well-placed to harness these disruptions and turn them into opportunities for our companies and people.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Charles Chong asked about the Government's efforts to build up our startup landscape.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Startups play an important role in our economy because they are nimble.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They churn over ideas quickly and are more willing to take risks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Over the past decade, there have been considerable efforts by various stakeholders to develop a thriving startup scene in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These include nurturing an entrepreneurial culture, providing funding support and catering for the necessary infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a result, we have seen a sizeable increase in both the number and the quality of our startups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In terms of quality, our startups have also improved with significant increases in the number and aggregate valuations of startup exits.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Notable successes include live customer support chat solution provider Zopim and online marketplace Lazada, which were acquired for about US$30 million in 2014 and US$1 billion in 2016 respectively.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Our efforts have catalysed a robust startup ecosystem here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But we can do more and we should.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I co-led a startup deep dive as part of the CFE discussions last year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We studied how to give our startup scene an additional push so that it can take off in a much larger way.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will, therefore, strengthen our startup support in three key areas, namely, (a) branding, (b) funding and (c) talent attraction.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A coherent brand identity for Singapore startups that resonates among Singaporeans and the rest of the world is important, given the fierce global competition for entrepreneurial talent and funding today.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some of the schemes under the Startup SG umbrella branding include: (a) Startup SG Founder to support first-time entrepreneurs; (b) Startup SG Tech to support the development of deep-tech innovations; (c) Startup SG Equity to incentivise equity co-investment for startups; (d) Startup SG Accelerator to support incubators and accelerators which offer programmes for startups; and (e) Startup SG Talent to support talent development for startups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: With the unified branding, it will be easier for budding entrepreneurs to identify the relevant schemes for their unique situation and their needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Over time, we will work with other stakeholders to further strengthen this Startup SG brand.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To further support our startups, we will also enhance two key enablers: first, funding and, secondly, talent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Equity financing is important to enable our startups to grow and scale.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, not all startups have the same funding needs or gestation periods.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For instance, compared to infocomm technology (ICT) startups that develop online applications or web portals, startups that develop non-ICT or deep technologies typically require higher capital outlays and a much longer gestation period to succeed, due to the prototyping process and product trials that they need to undergo.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, as part of the Startup SG Equity scheme, we will enhance the Government's co-investment support for promising startups in deep-tech areas, such as in medical technology, clean technology and advanced manufacturing, to catalyse private sector investment for this group.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will enhance the Government's support in two ways.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This enhancement allows the Government to tier our funding support for ICT and deep-tech startups according to their differing needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Mr Charles Chong noted, we need a strong talent pool, comprising capable entrepreneurs who can contribute to our local startup scene.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Given Singapore's small size, we need to remain open to promising global talent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The rising global protectionist sentiments that emerged in 2016 present us with the opportunity to position Singapore as an attractive startup location for global talent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Foreign entrepreneurs have the capacity to add to the vibrancy of our startup scene.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They complement our local startups through the cross-fertilisation of ideas, catalyse new partnerships and create good jobs for our people.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As of 2015, foreign startups employed more than 19,000 workers in total.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In 2003, we introduced a work pass scheme known as EntrePass for foreign entrepreneurs keen to start a business in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will further enhance this scheme to create a more conducive environment for promising global talent keen to establish innovative businesses here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Under the enhancements, the existing entry and renewal criteria will be revised.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In other words, if the foreign entrepreneur can demonstrate progress at the end of the first year, the EntrePass will be extended for another year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Thereafter, subsequent EntrePass renewals will be valid for two years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These enhancements will better position us to engage and attract a larger talent pool at the global setting at an earlier stage who can contribute to the vibrancy of our local startup scene.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The enhancements are especially timely, given the increasing international interest in Singapore as a global startup destination.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the same spirit of remaining open, we want to encourage our local startups to also adopt a global mindset and tap on our existing extensive bilateral networks as launching pads for their overseas ventures.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: GIA, mentioned by the Ministers for Trade and Industry Lim Hng Kiang and S Iswaran, seeks to enable this exchange of innovative ideas between our local companies and their foreign counterparts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, our local partners are already actively facilitating such collaborations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Last year, the Action Community for Entrepreneurship (ACE), a private-led initiative aimed at fostering entrepreneurship, also partnered US-based Singaporean networks to establish the ACE-Silicon Valley Chapter.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Both of these serve as platforms for our companies to gain access to US markets by tapping the experience and networks of US-based Singaporeans and their US counterparts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: GIA will ride on existing initiatives such as these to enable our companies to strengthen inroads, build partnerships in foreign markets and prepare our companies to internationalise.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Thomas Chua, Ms K Thanaletchimi, Ms Sun Xueling and Ms Cheryl Chan asked about the Government's role in supporting companies in their internationalisation efforts, particularly in emerging regions which are experiencing higher growth rates.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As the Minister for Trade Lim Hng Kiang mentioned, internationalisation is a key engine of growth and transformation for our companies, big and small.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To scale and transform, our companies must leverage the strong Singapore brand to tap good growth opportunities beyond our shores.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: IE Singapore supports companies looking to internationalise through various grant schemes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These include the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) for companies taking their first steps in internationalisation, and the Global Company Partnership (GCP) which provides more customised help for companies with a more established presence overseas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Notably, a significant share of these projects was oriented towards helping companies understand market needs, build track record in new markets or new lines of businesses, leverage digital platforms and channels to access global customers and scale-up, and level up capabilities through technology acquisition and overseas partnership and HR development.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Such efforts strengthen the credibility and business reputation of our companies and reinforce their ability to clinch future deals.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Miss Cheryl Chan pointed out, there are substantial growth opportunities in emerging economies which are experiencing higher growth on the back of rapid urbanisation and consumerism.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The focus of our company assistance has, indeed, been on emerging markets.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As the Minister for Industry S Iswaran mentioned, we will strengthen coordination of our agencies' overseas operations under the "Singapore Centres".

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will also continue to deepen our in-market presence and networks in these markets and help our companies identify and seize new opportunities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Additionally, we have several G-to-G projects in overseas markets to help our companies collaborate with in-market partners.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One such G-to-G project is CCI, which has allowed our companies to make inroads into the less familiar region of western China.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One company that has collaborated successfully with its Chongqing counterpart under the ambit of CCI is Changi Airports International (CAI), which agreed in January 2017 to form a commercial joint venture with the Chongqing Airport Group to manage the non-aeronautical business at Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As part of CCI, the Singapore Government is also working with our Chinese counterparts to develop the Southern Transport Corridor.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When ready, the Southern Transport Corridor will boost connectivity between western China and Southeast Asia via Guangxi, a province that has been designated as China's gateway to ASEAN, by shortening the transit time for goods between both regions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In complementing the Chinese plans to develop the western regions, we can open up even more new opportunities for our companies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Two companies are riding this wave of opportunity in Guangxi.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They are PSA International and Pacific International Lines (PIL).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They are currently partnering the Beibu Gulf Port Group to manage port facilities in Qinzhou, which is a key port for international lines and shipments to enter China from the south-west coast.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In September last year, I led a delegation to Nanning to support Singapore's participation at the annual China-ASEAN Expo (CAEXPO), a high-level platform that promotes economic cooperation between ASEAN and China.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is a Singapore company that specialises in mini cupcakes, Tian Tian Wu.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Two years ago, the founder had the opportunity to participate in the Singapore Pavilion at CAEXPO.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Shortly after, it started to grow its cupcake business in Nanning.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, Tian Tian Wu has three outlets in Nanning, all served by a central kitchen.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I understand that Tian Tian Wu's mini cupcakes are exceptionally popular among children and that parents are assured of the quality and safety due to the Singapore branding.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Tian Tian Wu has since expanded its service offerings to include cupcake baking classes for families.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As these companies have shown, there are plenty of opportunities for our companies in diverse sectors arising from the rapid growth of emerging regions around the world.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I encourage our companies to take advantage of the available Government support to capture these opportunities and reach greater heights of success.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Cases that involve criminal activity will be handled by the Police.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I have elaborated in my speech, there are plenty of opportunities for our companies and people, be they manufacturing firms looking to adopt technologies, SMEs keen on expanding overseas, or aspiring entrepreneurs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Through our various initiatives and programmes, the Government will support our companies and people to seize these opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, the Ministers for Trade and Industry have spoken about the political developments, economic trends and technological changes that will have an impact on our economy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singaporeans are naturally concerned about jobs and whether their skills will continue to be relevant.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We would like to assure Singaporeans that we will do our utmost to empower every Singaporean with the capabilities to make a good living.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will equip our people with skills, enable companies to develop their employees and expand our people's horizons to access opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Saktiandi Supaat that continuous education should be purposeful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the ITMs, the Government will collaborate with industry partners, TACs as well as unions to prepare our companies and people for the challenges and opportunities of each of the 23 industries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Possible career pathways and occupations are being charted out even as industries and jobs transform.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singaporeans have a diversity of initiatives under SkillsFuture to stay equipped and relevant.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Mr Suresh Dakshnamoorthy started his career in a marine and offshore company providing quality control of electrical equipment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Six years ago, he made a career switch to Thales, an aerospace company.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Although Suresh was unfamiliar with the aviation industry, Thales recognised his skills in electrical inspection as well as his familiarity with quality control tools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Suresh is now a Cell Leader in charge of planning production flows to meet his team's weekly targets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we can see from Suresh's example that when we identify common or complementary skillsets within a cluster of industries, we can help our people, our Singaporeans, to take advantage of adjacent employment opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Thirdly, we will build up a pipeline of local talent to access growth opportunities overseas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Supaat also asked how we can help our local businesses tap on infrastructure-related opportunities in Asia.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More details will be made known in the next quarter of this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides equipping our workforce, we will continue to enable companies to actively develop their workers' capabilities and skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will, in turn, better support their business objectives, be it to improve productivity, go digital or expand overseas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government's SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) offers support to companies that institutionalise programmes to build up leadership capability of Singaporeans, to develop our local bench strength and groom the next generation of Singaporean business leaders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through this programme, promising individuals gain exposure to key overseas market and critical business functions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in Mandarin.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   MTI recognises that some SMEs may need assistance to build up their HR and talent development capabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In this area, we encourage SMEs to tap on the SkillsFuture SME Mentors Programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: SME Mentors can work with you to establish structured learning and development (L&D) systems.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These systems can help improve the efficacy of your staff training, as well as uplift your capabilities to offer work-learn and internship places to young local talent.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about how micro-enterprises may face difficulty in training their employees due to limited resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) has been working with Post-Secondary Education Institutions (PSEIs) and training providers to deliver flexible and bite-sized training for working adults so that it is easier for them to undergo training.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, the Singapore Institute of Retail Studies (SIRS) provides bite-sized training that can be structured around business trading hours and conducted at the workplace.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: SIRS also delivers e-commerce courses and programmes for micro-enterprises.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Miss Chan that senior PMEs have a wealth of experience and we should tap on them as we build capabilities in our people and companies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we have 116 SkillsFuture SME mentors with extensive experience in various industries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Senior PMEs with strong industry knowledge and people management skills could help our companies develop HR capabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For PMEs with this aspiration, I encourage you to participate as a SkillsFuture SME Mentor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): The Ministers, Senior Minister of State and Minister of State have touched on the needs for companies to look for opportunities beyond our shores.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms Sun Xueling that apart from deep industry skills, our people need to have a global mindset to grasp emerging opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To nurture this global outlook, the Government is increasing the opportunities for Singaporeans to gain overseas exposure at different stages of their careers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For working adults, the SkillsFuture Study Award for International Business will enable them to acquire skillsets that are needed to navigate the complexities of overseas markets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The knowledge of our mother tongue languages has proven to be very useful in building our business and cultural relations in Asia and the neighbouring markets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We need the industries and unions to work hand in hand with us, as we support our companies and people on this journey of lifelong learning, training and development to stay ahead for the future.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We do have a little bit of time for some clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can you please avoid asking questions about chocolates, burgers or cupcakes at this hour?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I ask the Minister what sort of contractual amount we are looking at and how extensive this will be?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: In some jurisdictions, such schemes also come with some bridge financing for the startups, including for some new inventions, some safeguards for IP.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, is that what we are going to do as well for this scheme?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can I ask that the replies be kept short, too?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As for financing, I think we have a range of schemes available.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have to see whether that is adequate or there are special needs required.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Chairman, just two quick clarifications for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With regard to the lift companies under investigation, I understand there are a few more that are still under investigation for anti-competitive practices.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: When can we expect those investigations to be complete?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second clarification is with regard to the threshold before which interim measures are instituted against lift companies under investigation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I would suggest that it is not just the interest of the third-party lift manufacturers that the Competition Commission should be concerned about, but also the procurers of those services, like Town Councils, for whom lift costs have increased considerably.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for the Member's point about the interest of those who procure the services of the third-party lift maintenance contractors, the CCS had, indeed, in their press release, acknowledged that potential cost savings could be had if competition in the supply of lift spare parts was not curtailed.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is also something that they sought stakeholders' feedback on, and they take this feedback into consideration when deciding whether to accept the commitments that the company eventually undertook.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have a question for Minister of State Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: My question is in regard to the enhanced EntrePass scheme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And given that this is a startup, how would the officers assess the business plan?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in accepting him into the country as a startup, his business plan would have been taken into account as well, and all these will be taken holistically into consideration.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Are there any schemes or programmes right now which allow private sector personnel to be on secondment for short stints to MTI, or even another way around?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If not, is this something that MTI may consider for the future?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To the best of my knowledge, we do not have any formal scheme for the secondment of private sector individuals to the Ministry or our agencies per se.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I think the intent behind this suggestion was more that the private sector should be deeply involved in our economic planning and development processes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is something that is quite a pervasive system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If you look at the CFE process, more than 80% of the members in the main committee were from the private sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: When you go below that, the 9,000 people who were consulted were almost entirely from the private sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is a key part of the work.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the ITM process, we are involving businesses in a very intrinsic way, not just in the planning, but in the implementation, review, adaptation and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would add that we have a lot of secondment out from the public sector to the private sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I am not sure about the private sector to public agencies, because often the feedback is that they need more talent, not that they want to offer their talent to the public sector.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Iswaran for his answer on tiered electricity tariff.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Anecdotally, I heard of stories where certain expatriate families' utility bills are paid for by the companies, so they keep their aircon on throughout the day, throughout the whole house and the electricity bill can be more than a thousand dollars a month.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: So, it is exactly these few, I would say, which are the most polluting households, which we would like for them to pay a penalty to change their behaviour.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I assume the Member's focus is not just on expatriate families but, in general, on high consumers of electricity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In general, the right policy is to make sure everybody understands it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think we are all aware of that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You may be in a family in a 3-room flat, but you may be over-consuming.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And you may be in a family living in a condominium, but you may be under-consuming.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would suggest that the right approach is what we have embarked on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not perfect by any means, but it is, in general, a methodology that encourages conservation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If people are relying on their companies to pay the bill, then the company should look into their electricity consumption.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Chairman, as I remember, MTI does have an anti-profiteering taskforce that was set up some time back.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And given the concern about water hikes and how businesses could profiteer, these are concerns from the public whether the taskforce will now swing back into action and start to go around and ensure that there are no profiteering activities happening, especially in the neighbourhood areas?

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think Mr Liang is referring to the Committee against GST profiteering.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Actually, Mr Lee Yi Shyan can comment on this, because he used to be the Chair.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As the Member and also Mr Chairman has observed, the previous avatars this committee was really to address were something very generalised, like the Goods and Services Tax (GST) increase.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There was a concern then because the GST has a broad-based effect, and then you do have some concerns about how the tax, in turn, is transmitted through into prices.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the case of water, it is a very specific tax.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, if there are any reports of profiteering or suspected profiteering, that is something we are quite happy to see whether there is appropriate action that can be taken.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang, would you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I want to thank Minister Lim, Minister Iswaran, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Minister of State Koh Poh Koon and Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling for doing justice to the cuts that we have filed, with their very good and comprehensive answers.
